title: SSO provider lifecycle: no way to edit a provider (SAML certificate rotation means delete + re-register), and deleting a provider unlinks every user's SSO account and leaves its group mappings and grants behind
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, image built from cloud `main` `de8d979` (framework pin `e24136c2`), `OS_SSO_ENABLED=true`. Found in the live Okta run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3666 (real Okta developer org; SAML and OIDC apps; console driven in a browser).

## What happened
1. **No edit path for a provider.** Setup → SSO Providers → a SAML provider offers Request/Verify Domain, Delete, Edit Sign-In Options, Show/Edit Groups Claim. Nothing changes the IdP signing certificate, the IdP SSO URL, the entity id, or an OIDC client secret. `POST /sso/update-provider` exists but has no console door.
2. **Routine certificate rotation is therefore delete + re-register.** In Okta, a new signing key was generated and the SAML app switched to it. The next sign-in was refused `saml_error / Invalid SAML response`, as expected while the SP still holds the old certificate. The only console remedy was Delete SSO Provider, then Register SAML Provider with the **same provider id** and the new certificate, then re-enabling the sign-in options.
3. **Deleting a provider deletes every `sys_account` row of that provider.** After the re-register, the user who had signed in through it (`objectos-test3@example.com`, JIT-created by that provider) was refused `account_not_linked`. `sys_account` has no row for any of the three SSO users any more; the `sys_user` rows and their permission-set grants remain. A user with no local password is now locked out. Measured with `OS_SSO_DOMAIN_VERIFICATION=false`. Setting `sys_sso_provider.domain_verified = true` on the re-registered row (simulating a re-verified domain) did **not** re-link: the next sign-in was again `account_not_linked`. Behaviour with verification on and a real verified domain was not measured.
4. **Deletion leaves the provider's group mappings and projected grants.** After deleting `okta-oidc`, `sys_idp_group_mapping` still holds its row (`source_id okta-oidc`), and `sys_user_permission_set` still holds `viewer_readonly` grants with reason `sso-group-projection: provider 'okta-oidc'` for users who can no longer sign in through it.
5. **SSO group mappings have no console door.** Setup → IdP Group Mappings is a read-only "System-managed" list ("Entries appear automatically when their source action runs"). The only writer is `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/scim/set-group-mapping` (route ledger: "no SDK method builds this URL — an operator script posts it"). The mapping itself works: a JIT sign-in got `viewer_readonly` from the Okta group, for both OIDC and SAML.
6. **One email domain on two providers, silently.** `okta-saml` was registered for `example.com` while `okta-oidc` already held it. No warning was shown, and "Sign in with SSO" always routed to the first provider, with no way to reach the second.

## Expected
- An edit action per provider: SAML certificate (ideally two, for overlap), SSO URL, entity id; OIDC client id/secret, issuer, scopes; plus email/name attribute mapping (see the interop card).
- Deleting a provider either refuses while accounts are linked to it, or says how many users it unlinks and that they will be locked out. A re-registration with the same id should restore the links.
- Deleting a provider removes its mapping rows and the grants they projected (the projection marker makes this exact).
- A Setup form to add or remove a group → permission-set mapping for a provider.
- Registering a domain that another provider already serves is refused or warned.

## Steps
Register SAML provider `okta-saml` (Okta app) → JIT sign-in with a user → rotate the Okta app's signing key → sign-in is refused → Delete provider → Register again with the same id and new certificate → enable JIT and IdP-initiated → sign in as the same user → `account_not_linked`.
